card.name: Last word of common idioms
card.fires_on: The final word of a set phrase or idiom in general web text, such as 'whatever it takes', 'enough is enough' or 'one thing after another'. It also fires on short answer words after a question.

modes.label: Idiom endings
modes.description: The closing word of a fixed saying where the word is predictable from the earlier words.
modes.example: History is just “one thing after<< another>>”—in the words of Macbeth,

modes.label: Short answer or rhetorical word
modes.description: A single word that ends a question or answers it, like 'matter' or 'Yes'.
modes.example: What does it<< matter>>? Putting the pieces of the puzzle together

card.plain: It marks the last word of a familiar saying, where the ending is easy to guess.
